second_order: planning the FIRST logo and grid
theme_note: These passages all turn a wish to leave a mark into a drawable design: choosing the logo, making and shrinking its grid, and asking that the target and coordinates be posted. What varies is whether participants choose, draw, revise, or publish the plan.

second_order: calling people in and directing their help
theme_note: These passages recruit labour or direct willing helpers to a post, coordinate, Discord channel, link, or instruction. They vary from volunteering and promising later help to urgent calls and practical troubleshooting.

second_order: finding room and moving clear of neighbours
theme_note: These passages choose where the drawing can fit and relocate it when other work or Poland occupies the space. They vary between proposing treaties, preferring empty-looking space, announcing moves, and publishing moved coordinates or code.

second_order: building, repairing, and keeping the logo up
theme_note: These passages do the ongoing canvas work: starting, extending, repairing, watching, changing vandalised letters, and using bots or scripts for upkeep. What varies is manual versus automated work and construction versus maintenance under attack.

These passages treat the drawing as achieved or recognisable: saying it is almost there, declaring it done, claiming r/FRC made its mark, or finding the subreddit through the logo. They vary between progress cheers, completion claims, and recognition by viewers.

second_order: making room with neighbours and repairing relations
theme_note: These passages handle coexistence around the drawing: leaving a harmless corner, confronting damage, apologising, making alliances and treaties, returning overwritten work, and calming conflict. They vary from border design and diplomacy to mistakes, refusals, and apologies.

second_order: arguing whether scripts spoil place or keep it alive
theme_note: These passages openly contest scripted placement: calling it scummy or not gracious, defending it as necessary against destruction, reporting bot use, or taunting and minimizing how many scripted. What varies is the moral objection, practical defence, and retrospective accounting.

second_order: calling off repairs when place ended
theme_note: These passages announce the shutdown or move from impossible repair calls to recognising that pixels can no longer be changed. They vary between factual ending notices, late pleas, understated replies, and frustrated realization.

second_order: mourning the loss and arguing who ruined it
theme_note: These passages recount the damaged ending and assign or contest responsibility. What holds them together is participants making sense of loss; what varies is blame placed on Poland, rogues, Gwent, team 4611, abandonment, colour infighting, or scripting.

second_order: saving a preferred picture of what they made
theme_note: These passages preserve, repost, celebrate, or edit a preferred account of the finished drawing. They vary between calling it accurate or finest, correcting a repost, marvelling at team visibility, and photoshopping what the final image was supposed to be.

second_order: trying the FIRST logo again on Pxls.space
theme_note: These passages answer disappointment by proposing a successor canvas, asking where to build, and supplying a new starting coordinate. They vary between presenting the venue, explaining why to redo the lost logo, and beginning practical coordination.
